intended_object: Given an R-algebra homomorphism f : A → B whose values pairwise commute, the induced R-algebra homomorphism Aᵐᵒᵖ → B, x ↦ f(unop x). Inferred from the docstring and name.
explanation: The ring-homomorphism structure comes from RingHom.fromOpposite, which uses the commutation hypothesis: f(b·a) = f(b)·f(a) = f(a)·f(b). The underlying map is f ∘ unop. Compatibility with scalars follows from f.commutes, since the algebra map into Aᵐᵒᵖ is the one into A composed with op. The commutation hypothesis is exactly what multiplicativity needs, so it is not an extra condition. The setting (commutative semiring R, semirings A and B with R-algebra structures) is the natural one for algebra homomorphisms. The section variables S, IsScalarTower and so on are not used by the definition, so they are not included as hypotheses. RingHom.fromOpposite is the ring-homomorphism analogue that this definition builds on, not the same object, so no separate counterpart is given.
